commit.message:
security: validate $match/$project field paths against allowed_models/exclude_fields

_parse_match() and _interpret_projection() built their field paths straight
from caller input and passed them to Q()/values() with no check against
get_published_models() or get_excluded_fields() - both of those allowlists
were only ever consulted for $lookup and for building the advertised schema,
never at query execution time.

Since the whole left-hand side of a $match key is caller-controlled, this
also let a Django lookup/transform be smuggled in via the field name itself
(e.g. author__password__startswith), bypassing the $-operator allowlist a
few lines above it.

Net effect: an MCP client that can query one published model can traverse
any FK/M2M/reverse relation from it - including into models that were never
registered with a ModelQueryToolset at all - and use equality/startswith/
regex filters as a character-level read oracle over any field it finds,
including fields explicitly listed in exclude_fields. Publishing a single
model whose rows relate (even transitively) to auth.User is enough to read
out password hashes one character at a time.

This adds _validate_field_path(), mirroring the existing _validate_lookup()/
_resolve_model_from_path() logic already used for $lookup: walk the
'__'-separated path hop by hop, require each hop to be a real field, refuse
a relation hop into an unpublished model, and refuse any hop that is an
excluded field. It's threaded through _parse_match (including its $and/$or/
$nor recursion) and _interpret_projection, since $project turned out to have
the identical gap. The no-$project default output path now also builds its
field list from the model's concrete fields minus excluded_fields, so
exclude_fields actually keeps a field out of the response and not only out
of the schema shown to the model.

Verified against a PoC (one published Article model, unpublished auth.User):
the intended query is unaffected, internal_note/author_id no longer appear
in the default response body, and every traversal/exclusion/operator-in-
field-name attempt is now rejected with a clear ValueError.

Reported privately to the maintainer; this PR accompanies that report.

Resolve exclude_fields per related model and reject unresolved lookup segments

Addresses review feedback on the field-path validation added in the
previous commit:

- excluded_fields is now re-resolved at each hop via query_tool_models,
  so a related model's own exclude_fields is honoured once the path
  traverses into it, not just the root model's. A related model that
  passes the allowed_models check but has no registered toolset fails
  closed instead of being treated as having no exclusions.

- A path segment that does not resolve to a real model field (a Django
  lookup/transform such as __startswith or __year smuggled into the bare
  key) is now rejected outright instead of silently returning, which
  previously let any lookup bypass the $-operator allowlist on any
  already-published field.

Verified against a local project with two published, related toolsets
(one declaring its own exclude_fields): the related-model exclusion and
the lookup-suffix rejection are both enforced, while legitimate
traversal into non-excluded related fields and the $regex/extended
operator mechanisms are unaffected.
